title: Only Mammals Make Milk. This Egg-Laying Animal Does Too
subject: caecilian

scenes.text: Only mammals make milk. This egg-laying animal didn't get the memo.
It's a caecilian, a legless, nearly blind amphibian from Brazil. It looks like a worm.
Its babies squeak and nibble at their mother's rear. She lifts her body and releases a fat-rich fluid, up to six times a day.
This goes on for two months. In the first week alone, the hatchlings gain up to 130 percent of their mass.
The fluid comes from glands in her oviduct that swell while she raises them. Scientists published it in Science in 2024.
They also nibble her skin every few days, but the milk likely does most of the work. Only mammals make milk? Not anymore.

description:
Only mammals make milk. Not quite.
The ringed caecilian, a legless Brazilian amphibian, feeds its hatchlings a fat-rich fluid from glands in its oviduct, up to six times a day for two months.
Did you know any other animal could do this? Tell us below.
first_comment: Which animal would you have bet could never make milk? Mammals thought they owned it.
